title: Signed merchant requests for a billing API
name: Merchant signature authentication

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this middleware authenticates merchant requests? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A merchant's key is revoked (revoked_at set) while a request signed with it is in flight. What happens to requests that arrive after the revocation commits?
choices: They succeed until the 300-second tolerance window expires
They are rejected with 401 because findActive filters out revoked keys
They are rejected with 503 because the lookup throws
They succeed because the signature is still mathematically valid

questions.prompt: Why does the app capture `rawBody` in the express.json `verify` hook instead of signing `JSON.stringify(req.body)`?
choices: Because JSON.stringify is too slow for payment payloads
Because express.json discards the body after parsing
Because re-serialising parsed JSON can change key order, whitespace, or number formatting, so the HMAC would not match the bytes the merchant signed

questions.prompt: If the database is unreachable during key lookup, how does the middleware respond, and why does that matter?
choices: 401, so clients treat it as bad credentials and stop retrying
It calls next() so charges are not blocked by an auth outage
It throws and Express returns a default 500 with a stack trace
503 auth_unavailable, so an outage is distinguishable from bad credentials and the request is never let through
